guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.title: Wedding Seating Chart: Table Sizes and Group Rules
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.desc: How to build a wedding seating plan from RSVPs: table capacities, family politics, kids, plus-ones and a buffer for last-minute changes.
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.lead: Start only after RSVPs close. A seating chart built on an estimate has to be rebuilt, and every rebuild breaks something else.
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.f1v: Round tables of 8 or 10; long banquet tables of 12–20
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.f2v: Traditionally the couple, attendants and parents
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.f3v: Leave one or two spare places if the venue allows
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.f4v: One per guest, alphabetised; place cards one per seat
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.s1: Group people by relationship first, then fit groups to tables, then handle the leftovers. Keep a note of who needs a high chair, wheelchair access, a vegetarian meal or an early exit. Put the people who may need to leave quickly near an exit, and keep the speakers and anyone in the wedding party within sight of the top table.
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.s2: US receptions usually assign every guest a table, and a sweetheart table for just the couple is common. UK weddings more often have a formal top table with a defined seating order and a separate evening guest list that may not be seated at all. At large South Asian and Middle Eastern weddings, seating is frequently by family group with open or buffet service, and a rigid place-card plan can work against the flow.
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.s3: Avoid splitting a couple from their plus-one, seating divorced parents together without asking, and using tables at full capacity so a late change has nowhere to go. Check the actual table diameter with the venue — a '10-top' with a large centrepieces and ten place settings can be uncomfortably tight. Print a spare copy for the catering lead.
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.q1: When should we make the seating chart?
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.a1: After RSVPs close and the final headcount is confirmed, usually one to two weeks before the wedding.
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.q2: Do we need assigned seats or assigned tables?
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.a2: Assigned tables with free choice of seat is easier and less fragile. Full place cards are worth it for a formal plated meal with pre-selected courses.
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.q3: How do we handle children at the table?
guides.wedding-seating-chart-maker.a3: Confirm ages with parents, count high chairs in the table capacity, and keep families with young children near an exit and away from speakers.
